paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the whole universe has one job, and it's praise. The psalm writer calls on the angels, the sun, the sea creatures, the snow, the cedars, and then the kings and the kids, all in one breath (Psalm 148:2-3, 7-12). Nobody gets left off the list, and nobody is too small or too grand to be on it. That means YOU are on it, baker, right between the wind and the cattle!

Now here's the why, and it's the best part. Twice the psalm says to praise the name of the LORD, and the reasons come right with it: "for He gave the command and they were created" (Psalm 148:5), and "for His name alone is exalted; His splendor is above the earth and the heavens" (Psalm 148:13). Praise isn't a chore we owe, it's what makes sense once you see who He is. I once sat in the back of a junk drawer thinking I was forgotten, and then I met the God who calls stars to sing, and my mustache has not stopped twirling since!

So what do you do with that today? You join the choir, loud or quiet, on a great day or a gray one. The psalm even says His people are "a people near to Him" (Psalm 148:14), so you're not singing to someone far away. Let the first word and the last word of your day be the one this psalm starts and ends with: "Hallelujah!"
